title: Split Pea Soup

items.raw: 1 pound (2¼ cups) dried green split peas, picked over and rinsed
1 meaty ham bone, or 1 smoked ham hock, or 8 ounces diced smoked ham
2 tablespoons unsalted butter or olive oil
8 cups water or light chicken stock
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

steps.text: Melt the butter in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots, and celery and cook 8 to 10 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute more.
Stir in the split peas, the ham bone or hock, the water, bay leaves, and marjoram. Hold off on salt until the end — a ham bone can carry a great deal of it.

Bring to a boil, then reduce to a lazy simmer and cook, partly covered, 1¼ to 1½ hours. Stir every 20 minutes and scrape the bottom; split peas settle and scorch given the chance. The soup is ready when the peas have completely broken down and lost their shape.
Lift out the bone or hock. Pull off any meat, chop it, and stir it back into the pot. Discard the bone, skin, and fat, along with the bay leaves.
Leave it as is for a rustic soup, or purée part or all of it with an immersion blender. It will keep thickening as it stands, so thin with hot water to the consistency you want.
Now add salt to taste, plenty of black pepper, and — the step people skip — a teaspoon or two of red wine vinegar, which wakes the whole pot up.

notes.label: No soaking
notes.text: split peas do not need it and cook to mush in about 90 minutes regardless.

notes.label: Vegetarian
notes.text: skip the ham, use a good vegetable stock, and add 1 teaspoon of smoked paprika plus an extra splash of vinegar.

notes.label: Ahead of time
notes.text: excellent on day two and freezes for 3 months. It sets nearly solid when cold; thin it with water when reheating.

notes.label: To serve
notes.text: croutons fried in butter, or a spoonful of sour cream and a grind of pepper.

openQuestion: Whose soup is this, and is it the traditional after-Easter or after-Christmas ham-bone soup? Tell me if it gets puréed smooth or left chunky.
